result.summary: This residential intersection is characterized by a complete lack of dedicated pedestrian infrastructure, with no sidewalks or marked crosswalks visible. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with vehicular traffic, and the wide street geometry may encourage higher speeds in a residential setting.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways, forcing pedestrians to walk on the grass or in the roadway shared with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the visible streets

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks or signage, providing no designated or protected space for pedestrians to cross.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct concrete sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide physical separation between pedestrians and motor vehicles.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps at the intersection to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement traffic calming measures such as speed humps or curb extensions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential area.

result.summary: This residential intersection lacks essential pedestrian infrastructure, including marked crosswalks and curb ramps. The wide, unmarked pavement increases exposure time for pedestrians, while parked vehicles near the corners create potential sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks at this intersection fails to designate a safe path for pedestrians and reduces driver awareness.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The lack of sloped transitions at the corners creates a physical barrier for pedestrians with mobility aids or strollers.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corners can hide pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side curb and far left corner

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve visibility.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps at all crossing points to provide universal access and meet safety standards.

interventions.title: Corner Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement parking restrictions near the intersection to clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: A residential street environment with sidewalks but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control infrastructure. The wide roadway and parked vehicles near the corner increase pedestrian exposure and limit visibility between road users.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The lack of marked crosswalks at a wide intersection increases pedestrian exposure and fails to designate right-of-way.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the corner block sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks to clearly designate pedestrian paths and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corner to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: A residential intersection featuring continuous sidewalks and curb ramps, but lacking marked crosswalks or pedestrian-specific signage. The environment is generally low-speed, though parked vehicles near the corner create potential sightline obstructions.
